readings.text: <v>1</v> “For behold, the day is coming, burning like an oven, when all the arrogant and all evildoers will be stubble. The day that is coming shall set them ablaze, says the Lord of hosts, so that it will leave them neither root nor branch. <v>2</v> But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings. You shall go out leaping like calves from the stall. <v>3</v> And you shall tread down the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet, on the day when I act, says the Lord of hosts. <v>4</v> “Remember the law of my servant Moses, the statutes and rules that I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel. <v>5</v> “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and awesome day of the Lord comes. <v>6</v> And he will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a decree of utter destruction.”

<v>12</v> When it was day, the Jews made a plot and bound themselves by an oath neither to eat nor drink till they had killed Paul. <v>13</v> There were more than forty who made this conspiracy. <v>14</v> They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have strictly bound ourselves by an oath to taste no food till we have killed Paul. <v>15</v> Now therefore you, along with the council, give notice to the tribune to bring him down to you, as though you were going to determine his case more exactly. And we are ready to kill him before he comes near.” <v>16</v> Now the son of Paul’s sister heard of their ambush, so he went and entered the barracks and told Paul. <v>17</v> Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the tribune, for he has something to tell him.” <v>18</v> So he took him and brought him to the tribune and said, “Paul the prisoner called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, as he has something to say to you.” <v>19</v> The tribune took him by the hand, and going aside asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?” <v>20</v> And he said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though they were going to inquire somewhat more closely about him. <v>21</v> But do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty of their men are lying in ambush for him, who have bound themselves by an oath neither to eat nor drink till they have killed him. And now they are ready, waiting for your consent.” <v>22</v> So the tribune dismissed the young man, charging him, “Tell no one that you have informed me of these things.”

<v>5</v> In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah. And he had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth. <v>6</v> And they were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and statutes of the Lord. <v>7</v> But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years. <v>8</v> Now while he was serving as priest before God when his division was on duty, <v>9</v> according to the custom of the priesthood, he was chosen by lot to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense. <v>10</v> And the whole multitude of the people were praying outside at the hour of incense. <v>11</v> And there appeared to him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense. <v>12</v> And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him. <v>13</v> But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John. <v>14</v> And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth, <v>15</v> for he will be great before the Lord. And he must not drink wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb. <v>16</v> And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God, <v>17</v> and he will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just, to make ready for the Lord a people prepared.” <v>18</v> And Zechariah said to the angel, “How shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.” <v>19</v> And the angel answered him, “I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news. <v>20</v> And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day that these things take place, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.” <v>21</v> And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they were wondering at his delay in the temple. <v>22</v> And when he came out, he was unable to speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he kept making signs to them and remained mute. <v>23</v> And when his time of service was ended, he went to his home. <v>24</v> After these days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and for five months she kept herself hidden, saying, <v>25</v> “Thus the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked on me, to take away my reproach among people.”

<v>13</v> “You shall not oppress your neighbor or rob him. The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you all night until the morning. <v>14</v> You shall not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God: I am the Lord. <v>15</v> “You shall do no injustice in court. You shall not be partial to the poor or defer to the great, but in righteousness shall you judge your neighbor. <v>16</v> You shall not go around as a slanderer among your people, and you shall not stand up against the life of your neighbor: I am the Lord. <v>17</v> “You shall not hate your brother in your heart, but you shall reason frankly with your neighbor, lest you incur sin because of him. <v>18</v> You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the sons of your own people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the Lord.

<v>19</v> I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be cheered by news of you. <v>20</v> For I have no one like him, who will be genuinely concerned for your welfare. <v>21</v> For they all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ. <v>22</v> But you know Timothy’s proven worth, how as a son with a father he has served with me in the gospel. <v>23</v> I hope therefore to send him just as soon as I see how it will go with me, <v>24</v> and I trust in the Lord that shortly I myself will come also.

<v>25</v> And behold, a lawyer stood up to put him to the test, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” <v>26</v> He said to him, <red>“What is written in the Law? How do you read it?”</red> <v>27</v> And he answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.” <v>28</v> And he said to him, <red>“You have answered correctly;</red><red>do this, and you will live.”</red> <v>29</v> But he, desiring to justify himself, said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?” <v>30</v> Jesus replied, <red>“A man</red><red>was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who stripped him and beat him and departed, leaving him half dead.</red> <v>31</v> <red>Now by chance a</red><red>priest was going down that road, and when he saw him he passed by on the other side.</red> <v>32</v> <red>So likewise</red><red>a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.</red> <v>33</v> <red>But a</red><red>Samaritan, as he journeyed, came to where he was, and when he saw him, he had compassion.</red> <v>34</v> <red>He went to him and</red><red>bound up his wounds, pouring on</red><red>oil and wine. Then he set him on his own animal and brought him to an inn and took care of him.</red> <v>35</v> <red>And the next day he took out two</red><red>denarii</red> <red>and gave them to the innkeeper, saying, ‘Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.’</red> <v>36</v> <red>Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”</red> <v>37</v> He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” And Jesus said to him, <red>“You go, and do likewise.”</red>

<v>1</v> Praise the Lord! Sing to the Lord a new song, his praise in the assembly of the godly! <v>2</v> Let Israel be glad in his Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King! <v>3</v> Let them praise his name with dancing, making melody to him with tambourine and lyre! <v>4</v> For the Lord takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation. <v>5</v> Let the godly exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds. <v>6</v> Let the high praises of God be in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands, <v>7</v> to execute vengeance on the nations and punishments on the peoples, <v>8</v> to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron, <v>9</v> to execute on them the judgment written! This is honor for all his godly ones. Praise the Lord!

<v>10</v> Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace that was to be yours searched and inquired carefully, <v>11</v> inquiring what person or time the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating when he predicted the sufferings of Christ and the subsequent glories. <v>12</v> It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you, in the things that have now been announced to you through those who preached the good news to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look.

<v>21</v> In that same hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, <red>“I thank you, Father,</red><red>Lord of heaven and earth, that</red><red>you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and</red><red>revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for</red><red>such was your gracious will.</red> <v>22</v> <red>All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is</red><red>except the Father, or who the Father is</red><red>except the Son and anyone</red><red>to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.”</red> <v>23</v> Then turning to the disciples he said privately, <red>“Blessed are the eyes that see what you see!</red> <v>24</v> <red>For I tell you</red><red>that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.”</red>

<v>21</v> The man Elkanah and all his house went up to offer to the Lord the yearly sacrifice and to pay his vow. <v>22</v> But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “As soon as the child is weaned, I will bring him, so that he may appear in the presence of the Lord and dwell there forever.” <v>23</v> Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do what seems best to you; wait until you have weaned him; only, may the Lord establish his word.” So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him. <v>24</v> And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the Lord at Shiloh. And the child was young. <v>25</v> Then they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the child to Eli. <v>26</v> And she said, “Oh, my lord! As you live, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here in your presence, praying to the Lord. <v>27</v> For this child I prayed, and the Lord has granted me my petition that I made to him. <v>28</v> Therefore I have lent him to the Lord. As long as he lives, he is lent to the Lord.” And he worshiped the Lord there.

<v>1</v> What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? <v>2</v> By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it? <v>3</v> Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? <v>4</v> We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. <v>5</v> For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his. <v>6</v> We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin. <v>7</v> For one who has died has been set free from sin. <v>8</v> Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. <v>9</v> We know that Christ, being raised from the dead, will never die again; death no longer has dominion over him. <v>10</v> For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but the life he lives he lives to God. <v>11</v> So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.

<v>34</v> And calling the crowd to him with his disciples, he said to them, <red>“If anyone would come after me, let him</red><red>deny himself and</red><red>take up his cross and follow me.</red> <v>35</v> <red>For</red><red>whoever would save his life</red> <red>will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake</red><red>and the gospel’s will save it.</red> <v>36</v> <red>For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?</red> <v>37</v> <red>For</red><red>what can a man give in return for his soul?</red> <v>38</v> <red>For</red><red>whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this</red><red>adulterous and sinful generation, of him will the Son of Man also be ashamed</red><red>when he comes in the glory of his Father with</red><red>the holy angels.”</red>

<v>1</v> The Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying, <v>2</v> “Speak to the people of Israel and say to them, When you come into the land that I give you, the land shall keep a Sabbath to the Lord. <v>3</v> For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its fruits, <v>4</v> but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a Sabbath to the Lord. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard. <v>5</v> You shall not reap what grows of itself in your harvest, or gather the grapes of your undressed vine. It shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.

<v>20</v> And if you say, ‘What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we may not sow or gather in our crop?’ <v>21</v> I will command my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that it will produce a crop sufficient for three years. <v>22</v> When you sow in the eighth year, you will be eating some of the old crop; you shall eat the old until the ninth year, when its crop arrives. <v>23</v> “The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine. For you are strangers and sojourners with me.

<v>15</v> He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. <v>16</v> For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through him and for him. <v>17</v> And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together. <v>18</v> And he is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in everything he might be preeminent.

<v>22</v> And he said to his disciples, <red>“Therefore I tell you,</red><red>do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on.</red> <v>23</v> <red>For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.</red> <v>24</v> <red>Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and yet God feeds them.</red><red>Of how much more value are you than the birds!</red> <v>25</v> <red>And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his</red><red>span of life?</red> <v>26</v> <red>If then you are not able to do as small a thing as that, why are you anxious about the rest?</red> <v>27</v> <red>Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you,</red><red>even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.</red>

<v>20</v> And if you say, ‘What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we may not sow or gather in our crop?’ <v>21</v> I will command my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that it will produce a crop sufficient for three years.
<v>22</v> When you sow in the eighth year, you will be eating some of the old crop; you shall eat the old until the ninth year, when its crop arrives.

<v>15</v> He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. <v>16</v> For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through him and for him.

<v>17</v> And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together. <v>18</v> And he is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in everything he might be preeminent.

<v>11</v> And the vision of all this has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed. When men give it to one who can read, saying, “Read this,” he says, “I cannot, for it is sealed.” <v>12</v> And when they give the book to one who cannot read, saying, “Read this,” he says, “I cannot read.” <v>13</v> And the Lord said: “Because this people draw near with their mouth and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment taught by men, <v>14</v> therefore, behold, I will again do wonderful things with this people, with wonder upon wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the discernment of their discerning men shall be hidden.” <v>15</v> Ah, you who hide deep from the Lord your counsel, whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Who sees us? Who knows us?” <v>16</v> You turn things upside down! Shall the potter be regarded as the clay, that the thing made should say of its maker, “He did not make me”; or the thing formed say of him who formed it, “He has no understanding”? <v>17</v> Is it not yet a very little while until Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be regarded as a forest? <v>18</v> In that day the deaf shall hear the words of a book, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.

<v>16</v> Therefore let no one pass judgment on you in questions of food and drink, or with regard to a festival or a new moon or a Sabbath. <v>17</v> These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ. <v>18</v> Let no one disqualify you, insisting on asceticism and worship of angels, going on in detail about visions, puffed up without reason by his sensuous mind, <v>19</v> and not holding fast to the Head, from whom the whole body, nourished and knit together through its joints and ligaments, grows with a growth that is from God. <v>20</v> If with Christ you died to the elemental spirits of the world, why, as if you were still alive in the world, do you submit to regulations— <v>21</v> “Do not handle, Do not taste, Do not touch” <v>22</v> (referring to things that all perish as they are used)—according to human precepts and teachings? <v>23</v> These have indeed an appearance of wisdom in promoting self-made religion and asceticism and severity to the body, but they are of no value in stopping the indulgence of the flesh.

<v>1</v> Now when the Pharisees gathered to him, with some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem, <v>2</v> they saw that some of his disciples ate with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed. <v>3</v> (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands properly, holding to the tradition of the elders, <v>4</v> and when they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions that they observe, such as the washing of cups and pots and copper vessels and dining couches.) <v>5</v> And the Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat with defiled hands?” <v>6</v> And he said to them, <red>“Well did Isaiah prophesy of you</red><red>hypocrites, as it is written,</red> <red>“‘This people honors me with their lips,</red> <red>but their heart is far from me;</red> <v>7</v> <red>in vain do they worship me,</red> <red>teaching as</red> <red>doctrines the commandments of men.’</red> <v>8</v> <red>You leave the commandment of God and hold to the tradition of men.”</red> <v>9</v> And he said to them, <red>“You have a fine way of</red><red>rejecting the commandment of God in order to establish your tradition!</red> <v>10</v> <red>For Moses said,</red><red>‘Honor your father and your mother’; and,</red><red>‘Whoever reviles father or mother must surely die.’</red> <v>11</v> <red>But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever you would have gained from me is Corban”’ (that is, given to God)</red><red>—</red> <v>12</v> <red>then you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or mother,</red> <v>13</v> <red>thus</red><red>making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And many such things you do.”</red>
<v>15</v> Ah, you who hide deep from the Lord your counsel, whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Who sees us? Who knows us?”

<v>16</v> You turn things upside down! Shall the potter be regarded as the clay, that the thing made should say of its maker, “He did not make me”; or the thing formed say of him who formed it, “He has no understanding”?

<v>23</v> These have indeed an appearance of wisdom in promoting self-made religion and asceticism and severity to the body, but they are of no value in stopping the indulgence of the flesh.

<v>9</v> And he said to them, <red>“You have a fine way of</red><red>rejecting the commandment of God in order to establish your tradition!</red>

<v>1</v> Why, O Lord, do you stand far away? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble? <v>2</v> In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor; let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised. <v>3</v> For the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul, and the one greedy for gain curses and renounces the Lord. <v>4</v> In the pride of his face the wicked does not seek him; all his thoughts are, “There is no God.” <v>5</v> His ways prosper at all times; your judgments are on high, out of his sight; as for all his foes, he puffs at them. <v>6</v> He says in his heart, “I shall not be moved; throughout all generations I shall not meet adversity.” <v>7</v> His mouth is filled with cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue are mischief and iniquity. <v>8</v> He sits in ambush in the villages; in hiding places he murders the innocent. His eyes stealthily watch for the helpless; <v>9</v> he lurks in ambush like a lion in his thicket; he lurks that he may seize the poor; he seizes the poor when he draws him into his net. <v>10</v> The helpless are crushed, sink down, and fall by his might.

<v>7</v> Beloved, I am writing you no new commandment, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word that you have heard. <v>8</v> At the same time, it is a new commandment that I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining. <v>9</v> Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness. <v>10</v> Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no cause for stumbling. <v>11</v> But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes. <v>12</v> I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for his name’s sake. <v>13</v> I am writing to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, children, because you know the Father. <v>14</v> I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. <v>11</v> Therefore remember that at one time you Gentiles in the flesh, called “the uncircumcision” by what is called the circumcision, which is made in the flesh by hands— <v>12</v> remember that you were at that time separated from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world. <v>13</v> But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. <v>14</v> For he himself is our peace, who has made us both one and has broken down in his flesh the dividing wall of hostility <v>15</v> by abolishing the law of commandments expressed in ordinances, that he might create in himself one new man in place of the two, so making peace, <v>16</v> and might reconcile us both to God in one body through the cross, thereby killing the hostility.

<v>31</v> So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him, <red>“If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples,</red> <v>32</v> <red>and you will</red><red>know the truth, and the truth</red><red>will set you free.”</red> <v>33</v> They answered him, “We are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone. How is it that you say, ‘You will become free’?” <v>34</v> Jesus answered them, <red>“Truly, truly, I say to you,</red><red>everyone who practices sin is a slave</red> <red>to sin.</red> <v>35</v> <red>The slave does not remain in the house forever;</red><red>the son remains forever.</red> <v>36</v> <red>So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.</red> <v>37</v> <red>I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet</red><red>you seek to kill me because my word finds no place in you.</red> <v>38</v> <red>I speak of what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard</red><red>from your father.”</red> <v>39</v> They answered him, “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said to them, <red>“If you were Abraham’s children, you would be doing the works Abraham did,</red> <v>40</v> <red>but now</red><red>you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth</red><red>that I heard from God. It is because you cannot</red><red>bear to hear my word.</red> <v>44</v> <red>You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father’s desires.</red><red>He was a murderer from the beginning, and</red><red>does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him.</red><red>When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies.</red> <v>45</v> <red>But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.</red>

<v>4</v> From Mount Hor they set out by the way to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. And if a serpent bit anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.

<v>33</v> Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and how inscrutable his ways! <v>34</v> “For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counselor?” <v>35</v> “Or who has given a gift to him that he might be repaid?” <v>36</v> For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be glory forever. Amen.

<v>2</v> Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! <v>6</v> Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump? <v>7</v> Cleanse out the old leaven that you may be a new lump, as you really are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. <v>8</v> Let us therefore celebrate the festival, not with the old leaven, the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

<v>1</v> Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread drew near, which is called the Passover. <v>2</v> And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how to put him to death, for they feared the people. <v>3</v> Then Satan entered into Judas called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve. <v>4</v> He went away and conferred with the chief priests and officers how he might betray him to them. <v>5</v> And they were glad, and agreed to give him money. <v>6</v> So he consented and sought an opportunity to betray him to them in the absence of a crowd. <v>7</v> Then came the day of Unleavened Bread, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed. <v>8</v> So Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, <red>“Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat it.”</red> <v>9</v> They said to him, “Where will you have us prepare it?” <v>10</v> He said to them, <red>“Behold, when you have entered the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house that he enters</red> <v>11</v> <red>and tell the master of the house,</red><red>‘The Teacher says to you, Where is</red><red>the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’</red> <v>12</v> <red>And he will show you</red><red>a large upper room furnished; prepare it there.”</red> <v>13</v> And they went and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

<v>1</v> Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations. <v>2</v> He will not cry aloud or lift up his voice, or make it heard in the street; <v>3</v> a bruised reed he will not break, and a faintly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice. <v>4</v> He will not grow faint or be discouraged till he has established justice in the earth; and the coastlands wait for his law. <v>5</v> Thus says God, the Lord, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and what comes from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk in it: <v>6</v> “I am the Lord; I have called you in righteousness; I will take you by the hand and keep you; I will give you as a covenant for the people, a light for the nations, <v>7</v> to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.

<v>51</v> “You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you. <v>52</v> Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whom you have now betrayed and murdered, <v>53</v> you who received the law as delivered by angels and did not keep it.” <v>54</v> Now when they heard these things they were enraged, and they ground their teeth at him. <v>55</v> But he, full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. <v>56</v> And he said, “Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.” <v>57</v> But they cried out with a loud voice and stopped their ears and rushed together at him. <v>58</v> Then they cast him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul. <v>59</v> And as they were stoning Stephen, he called out, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” <v>60</v> And falling to his knees he cried out with a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

<v>39</v> And he came out and went, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed him. <v>40</v> And when he came to the place, he said to them, <red>“Pray that you may not</red><red>enter into temptation.”</red> <v>41</v> And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, and knelt down and prayed, <v>42</v> saying, <red>“Father, if you are willing, remove</red><red>this cup from me.</red><red>Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”</red> <v>43</v> And there appeared to him an angel from heaven, strengthening him. <v>44</v> And being in agony he prayed more earnestly; and his sweat became like great drops of blood falling down to the ground. <v>45</v> And when he rose from prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping for sorrow, <v>46</v> and he said to them, <red>“Why are you sleeping? Rise and</red><red>pray that you may not enter into temptation.”</red>

<v>1</v> Listen to me, O coastlands, and give attention, you peoples from afar. The Lord called me from the womb, from the body of my mother he named my name. <v>2</v> He made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me; he made me a polished arrow; in his quiver he hid me away. <v>3</v> And he said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” <v>4</v> But I said, “I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my right is with the Lord, and my recompense with my God.” <v>5</v> And now the Lord says, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him; and that Israel might be gathered to him— for I am honored in the eyes of the Lord, and my God has become my strength— <v>6</v> he says: “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to bring back the preserved of Israel; I will make you as a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”

<v>1</v> So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any participation in the Spirit, any affection and sympathy, <v>2</v> complete my joy by being of the same mind, having the same love, being in full accord and of one mind. <v>3</v> Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves. <v>4</v> Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others. <v>5</v> Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, <v>6</v> who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, <v>7</v> but emptied himself, by taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. <v>8</v> And being found in human form, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. <v>9</v> Therefore God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name,

<v>47</v> While he was still speaking, there came a crowd, and the man called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He drew near to Jesus to kiss him, <v>48</v> but Jesus said to him, <red>“Judas, would you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”</red> <v>49</v> And when those who were around him saw what would follow, they said, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?” <v>50</v> And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear. <v>51</v> But Jesus said, <red>“No more of this!”</red> And he touched his ear and healed him. <v>52</v> Then Jesus said to the chief priests and officers of the temple and elders, who had come out against him, <red>“Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?</red> <v>53</v> <red>When</red><red>I was with you day after day in the temple, you did not lay hands on me. But this is</red><red>your hour, and</red><red>the power of darkness.”</red>

<v>4</v> The Lord God has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with a word him who is weary. Morning by morning he awakens; he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught. <v>5</v> The Lord God has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I turned not backward. <v>6</v> I gave my back to those who strike, and my cheeks to those who pull out the beard; I hid not my face from disgrace and spitting. <v>7</v> But the Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame. <v>8</v> He who vindicates me is near. Who will contend with me? Let us stand up together. Who is my adversary? Let him come near to me. <v>9</v> Behold, the Lord God helps me; who will declare me guilty? Behold, all of them will wear out like a garment; the moth will eat them up.

<v>1</v> Then I looked, and behold, on Mount Zion stood the Lamb, and with him 144,000 who had his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads. <v>2</v> And I heard a voice from heaven like the roar of many waters and like the sound of loud thunder. The voice I heard was like the sound of harpists playing on their harps, <v>3</v> and they were singing a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and before the elders. No one could learn that song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth. <v>4</v> It is these who have not defiled themselves with women, for they are virgins. It is these who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These have been redeemed from mankind as firstfruits for God and the Lamb, <v>5</v> and in their mouth no lie was found, for they are blameless.

<v>54</v> Then they seized him and led him away, bringing him into the high priest’s house, and Peter was following at a distance. <v>55</v> And when they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them. <v>56</v> Then a servant girl, seeing him as he sat in the light and looking closely at him, said, “This man also was with him.” <v>57</v> But he denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know him.” <v>58</v> And a little later someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.” <v>59</v> And after an interval of about an hour still another insisted, saying, “Certainly this man also was with him, for he too is a Galilean.” <v>60</v> But Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are talking about.” And immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed. <v>61</v> And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the saying of the Lord, how he had said to him, <red>“Before the rooster crows today, you will</red><red>deny me three times.”</red> <v>62</v> And he went out and wept bitterly. <v>63</v> Now the men who were holding Jesus in custody were mocking him as they beat him. <v>64</v> They also blindfolded him and kept asking him, “Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?” <v>65</v> And they said many other things against him, blaspheming him. <v>66</v> When day came, the assembly of the elders of the people gathered together, both chief priests and scribes. And they led him away to their council, and they said, <v>67</v> “If you are the Christ, tell us.” But he said to them, <red>“If I tell you, you will not believe,</red> <v>68</v> <red>and if I ask you, you will not answer.</red> <v>69</v> <red>But from now on the Son of Man shall be seated</red><red>at the right hand of the power of God.”</red> <v>70</v> So they all said, “Are you the Son of God, then?” And he said to them, <red>“You say that I am.”</red> <v>71</v> Then they said, “What further testimony do we need? We have heard it ourselves from his own lips.”

<v>21</v> Then Moses called all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go and select lambs for yourselves according to your clans, and kill the Passover lamb. <v>22</v> Take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood that is in the basin. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning. <v>23</v> For the Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians, and when he sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the Lord will pass over the door and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike you. <v>24</v> You shall observe this rite as a statute for you and for your sons forever. <v>25</v> And when you come to the land that the Lord will give you, as he has promised, you shall keep this service. <v>26</v> And when your children say to you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’ <v>27</v> you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of the Lord’s Passover, for he passed over the houses of the people of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians but spared our houses.’” And the people bowed their heads and worshiped. <v>28</v> Then the people of Israel went and did so; as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

<v>20</v> When you come together, it is not the Lord’s supper that you eat. <v>21</v> For in eating, each one goes ahead with his own meal. One goes hungry, another gets drunk. <v>22</v> What! Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I commend you in this? No, I will not. <v>23</v> For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took bread, <v>24</v> and when he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, <red>“This is my body, which is for</red> <red>you. Do this in remembrance of me.”</red> <v>25</v> In the same way also he took the cup, after supper, saying, <red>“This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.”</red> <v>26</v> For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes. <v>27</v> Whoever, therefore, eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty concerning the body and blood of the Lord. <v>28</v> Let a person examine himself, then, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup. <v>29</v> For anyone who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on himself. <v>30</v> That is why many of you are weak and ill, and some have died. <v>31</v> But if we judged ourselves truly, we would not be judged. <v>32</v> But when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned along with the world.

<v>14</v> And when the hour came, he reclined at table, and the apostles with him. <v>15</v> And he said to them, <red>“I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.</red> <v>16</v> <red>For I tell you I will not eat it</red> <red>until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”</red> <v>17</v> And he took a cup, and when he had given thanks he said, <red>“Take this, and divide it among yourselves.</red> <v>18</v> <red>For I tell you that from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine</red><red>until the kingdom of God comes.”</red> <v>19</v> And he took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, <red>“This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”</red> <v>20</v> And likewise the cup after they had eaten, saying, <red>“This cup that is poured out for you is</red><red>the new</red><red>covenant in my blood.</red> <v>21</v> <red>But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is</red><red>with me on the table.</red> <v>22</v> <red>For the Son of Man goes</red><red>as it has been determined, but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!”</red> <v>23</v> And they began to question one another, which of them it could be who was going to do this.

<v>12</v> Many bulls encompass me; strong bulls of Bashan surround me; <v>13</v> they open wide their mouths at me, like a ravening and roaring lion. <v>14</v> I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint; my heart is like wax; it is melted within my breast; <v>15</v> my strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to my jaws; you lay me in the dust of death. <v>16</v> For dogs encompass me; a company of evildoers encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet— <v>17</v> I can count all my bones— they stare and gloat over me; <v>18</v> they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots. <v>19</v> But you, O Lord, do not be far off! O you my help, come quickly to my aid! <v>20</v> Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog! <v>21</v> Save me from the mouth of the lion! You have rescued me from the horns of the wild oxen!

<v>11</v> Therefore remember that at one time you Gentiles in the flesh, called “the uncircumcision” by what is called the circumcision, which is made in the flesh by hands— <v>12</v> remember that you were at that time separated from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world. <v>13</v> But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. <v>14</v> For he himself is our peace, who has made us both one and has broken down in his flesh the dividing wall of hostility <v>15</v> by abolishing the law of commandments expressed in ordinances, that he might create in himself one new man in place of the two, so making peace, <v>16</v> and might reconcile us both to God in one body through the cross, thereby killing the hostility.

<v>26</v> And as they led him away, they seized one Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, and laid on him the cross, to carry it behind Jesus. <v>27</v> And there followed him a great multitude of the people and of women who were mourning and lamenting for him. <v>28</v> But turning to them Jesus said, <red>“Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.</red> <v>29</v> <red>For behold,</red><red>the days are coming when they will say,</red><red>‘Blessed are the barren and the wombs that never bore and the breasts that never nursed!’</red> <v>30</v> <red>Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’</red> <v>31</v> <red>For</red><red>if they do these things when</red><red>the wood is green, what will happen</red><red>when it is dry?”</red> <v>32</v> Two others, who were criminals, were led away to be put to death with him. <v>33</v> And when they came to the place that is called The Skull, there they crucified him, and the criminals, one on his right and one on his left. <v>34</v> And Jesus said, <red>“Father,</red><red>forgive them,</red><red>for they know not what they do.”</red> And they cast lots to divide his garments. <v>35</v> And the people stood by, watching, but the rulers scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ of God, his Chosen One!” <v>36</v> The soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him sour wine <v>37</v> and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!” <v>38</v> There was also an inscription over him, “This is the King of the Jews.” <v>39</v> One of the criminals who were hanged railed at him, saying, “Are you not the Christ?
